question: Should autoreview accept these two named JavaScript/TypeScript roots as a narrow partial exception, or should this PR instead establish a general rule for safe non-literal references?
rationale: The patch appears safe for its tested shapes, but the linked issue requests a broader solution and the choice defines a secret-scanner boundary that automation should not set implicitly.

options.title: Land as partial fix
options.body: Approve the narrow dialect-scoped roots, remove the closing relationship, and leave the canonical issue open for the general cases.

options.title: Generalize reference detection
options.body: Expand this branch to recognize syntactically safe non-literal JavaScript/TypeScript references and add comprehensive negative security tests.

options.title: Keep existing boundary
options.body: Decline the new roots and document the currently supported reference shapes or redaction workflow.

recommendation.title: Land as partial fix
recommendation.body: Approve the narrow dialect-scoped roots, remove the closing relationship, and leave the canonical issue open for the general cases.
